kept.title: Laneways are salted, not plowed
kept.detail: Under the City's winter report, public laneways like Croft Street are only salted, within 24 hours after snowfall ends, and are not plowed. The report also says laneways often lack room to store snow, which can block access. A walk from a laneway home to a stop at night or early morning could start on an unplowed laneway.

cites.quote: The Council-approved winter maintenance service level for public laneways is salting only, within 24 hours after the end of snowfall, to manage icy conditions; snow plowing is not provided.
Public laneways are often too narrow and typically lack sufficient on-site snow storage capacity, creating the potential for snow to be pushed against garages and fences

kept.title: Sidewalk clearing starts at 2 cm and can take about 12 hours
kept.detail: The City starts clearing sidewalks once 2 cm of snow has built up. Crews usually finish a full cycle in about 12 hours, so some sidewalks may not be cleared yet at late-night or early-morning times after a snowfall. The report says TTC priority stops got focused clearing, but the data does not show whether the stops near Croft Street are on that list.

cites.quote: the City begins sidewalk clearing once snow accumulation reaches 2 cm.
City crews typically complete a full sidewalk clearing cycle within approximately 12 hours once accumulation reaches 2 cm.
the TTC provided a list of priority stops and routes, which helped focus clearing efforts on high- traffic and higher-risk locations.
